Meet with Tromml’s CEO

Investor Memo · October 2026 · Limited Angel Round

Some are using AI to replace sales teams. We use it to make them irreplaceable.

Despite every change in how an order gets placed, the automotive aftermarket is still driven by relationships. The sales teams who know they are selling trust as much as parts will keep winning in this half-trillion-dollar market. The problem is that almost none of what they know has ever made it into a system, so real AI has nowhere to start.

That gap is why we launched Minecart, a sales intelligence platform that tells reps which accounts need attention and what to talk about, captures the conversation that follows, and brings in automation to support the rep, not replace them. With Snap-on, 1-800-Radiator, Auto-Wares, and ACI Parts Plus on the client list, Tromml is growing from the tool its sales teams use into the foundation for how this industry uses AI across its revenue operations.

Traction

Minecart is less than a year old and has paying customers at every level of the industry: Snap-on, ACI Parts Plus, Auto-Wares, and 1-800-Radiator. We land small, giving managers visibility into the field team, then expand across the organization to every rep and into revenue operations.

That traction has opened a $3M+ pipeline, with Advance Auto Parts at final approval and proposals in 2027 budgets at Dorman Products and Niterra.

Our bet

The real work in this industry happens in the field, on the phone, and at the counter, and almost none of it gets written down. CRMs missed the mark. Reps filled out forms to feed a system of record that was stale the day it was entered and never shaped the next visit. Millions in market intel stayed in a rep’s head and a notebook.

AI changes that only for the companies that capture the knowledge first. They end up with the company brain, the system of action every AI tool in this industry will run on. We are building it for the aftermarket and commercial vehicle industry.

Why now

Every distributor and brand in this industry is being told to do something with AI, and consolidation is forcing them to do more with fewer people. The technology exists. What is missing is a record of what their customers say and what their reps do about it, so there is nothing for it to run on.

Minecart saves reps time (fast ROI), shows managers what is actually happening (better strategy and execution), and builds intelligence the company keeps (compounding value).

How it works

One example, start to finish. Marcus sells for a regional distributor. His manager’s priority this quarter is brakes.

1. For the rep

Minecart flags Ridgeline Auto Care: brake orders down a third in six weeks, and a counter call last week about European ceramic pads. It adds two stops on the same road and gives Marcus three talking points. The owner tells him three rotors on one part number came back warped, so brake jobs went to a competitor, and a second location opens in the spring. Back in the truck, Marcus records it in the app while it is fresh. No forms, no typing, no call reports. 

2. The manager

Monday, Ridgeline is at the top of the manager’s report with the reason: comebacks flagged as a product risk, pads as an opportunity, the new location as expansion. He pushes one question into every rep’s briefings: ask about rotor comebacks.

3. The company

Two weeks later, eleven shops have reported the same part number. Purchasing pauses the reorder. The product team has a defect pattern before warranty claims would show it. Marketing pulls the rotor promotion and gets every shop that asked about European pads. Every conversation sharpens the next briefing, and the loop compounds. Agents are not a separate product. They are how more of that work gets done, before anyone asks.

It works on calls too. Our first week with Snap-on turned up more than half a million dollars in sales leads sitting in their support calls.

4. The industry

The rotor comeback is not only the distributor’s problem. The rep agency that carries the line and the manufacturer that makes it both need to know, and today none of them hear it until the warranty claims land. With every tier running on the same shops, parts, and language, the issue moves up the chain the week it happens, and priorities and programs move back down the same way. One note, three companies acting on it. Get the aftermarket right and the same structure is waiting in electrical, plumbing and HVAC, and construction supply.

Market

Our customers’ markets top half a trillion dollars across light-duty, commercial vehicle, and powersports, and the same reps and distributors span all three. Almost nobody is building for them. The people moving billions in parts have no software that understands how they work. We do.

As the work shifts to agents, the value shifts with it. An agent that does the work captures the value of the work, and it is only as good as the context it runs on.

The same model fits the rest of industrial parts and supply: electrical, plumbing and HVAC, construction and home repair. Work is already underway in Europe.

Business model

  • Enter with the sales reps. Per-seat subscriptions for the field team, or a reporting fee if they want to start there. Runs beside the CRM they already have. An easy first yes.
  • Expand to every customer-facing team. Counter, store, delivery, and customer service capture on the same system, priced by seat and by location. Same conversations, now from every door the customer walks through.
  • Unlock reporting for the rest of the company. With the front line captured, marketing, product, purchasing, and leadership get their own reports from it. No new data entry, just more readers.
  • Automate the support teams. Agents run on that context: the follow-up drafted, the promotion pulled, the defect flagged to product, the forecast built from what customers are actually saying, not just what they bought.

Training is how we land, not a side business. Paid AI sessions at industry events cover much of our travel and turn those rooms into customers.
